Find the x-coordinates of the points of intersection of \( y=x^2-9x+22 \) and \( y=2 \).
pool.sol: Substituting the line into the curve gives \( x^2-9x+20=0 \), which factorises as \( (x-5)(x-4)=0 \), so \(x=4\) or \(x=5\).

Either \( x+4=2 \), giving \(x=-2\), or \( x+4=-2 \), giving \(x=-6\).

pool.text: Solve the inequality \( x^2-6x<0 \).
pool.sol: The quadratic factorises as \( x(x-6) \) with roots \(0\) and \(6\); since the parabola opens upward, the expression is < 0 between the roots, giving \( 0<x<6 \).
Either \( x-4=3 \), giving \(x=7\), or \( x-4=-3 \), giving \(x=1\).
\( |x-2|>7 \) means \( -7>x-2>7 \), so \( x<-5 \text{ or } x>9 \) (after subtracting -2 throughout).

pool.text: Solve the inequality \( x^2-4x-5>0 \).
pool.sol: The quadratic factorises as \( (x+1)(x-5) \) with roots \(-1\) and \(5\); since the parabola opens upward, the expression is > 0 outside the roots, giving \( x<-1 \text{ or } x>5 \).
Either \( x-3=4 \), giving \(x=7\), or \( x-3=-4 \), giving \(x=-1\).

pool.text: A particle of mass \( 14 \) kg slides down a rough plane inclined at \( 45^\circ \) to the horizontal, experiencing a constant friction force of \( 19 \) N. Taking \( g=9.8 \) m/s\(^2\), find its acceleration down the slope.
pool.sol: \( W=mg=14\times9.8=137.20 \) N. Component along slope \( =W\sin45^\circ\approx97.02 \) N. Net force \( \approx78.02 \) N. \( a=F/m\approx5.57 \) m/s\(^2\)
